label: Original-phase input of 1/x/m/n/f/0/z/j at early-middle positions, boosted by similar earlier tokens
explanation: Fires only during the original (input) phase: never at t=0, never on <DEL>, and essentially never in the copy phase (3 of 63k activations). Rate peaks at t=3-4 and drops off after t=6. It depends on the current input token: 1 is by far the strongest trigger (34% rate, 32% of mass, and the top of every max-activating example), then x, m, n, f, 0, z, j. It is stronger when the prefix already holds tokens from a similar set (z, 1, f, o, j, m, x, 0), e.g. f z 1 or z z 1 gives near-max activation. First occurrences dominate (84% of mass). Magnitude is modulated by token identity (1 is highest) and by how many trigger tokens came just before. It mostly does not fire on vowels, u, q, i, p or most other letters. Precision is limited: the token set and prefix conditions are graded, roughly additive effects rather than a sharp rule, so many predicted steps stay below threshold. Dev: P 0.58, R 0.77, F1 0.66, mass recall 0.87.
